canonical.title: Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes
canonical.sourceFilePath: 09. Heaps/3. Hard Problems/02. Minimum Cost to join n ropes.cpp

narrative.title: The Cable Splice Accounting
narrative.scenario: A utility crew must splice a pile of cables into one continuous line. Every splice fuses two runs into one whose length is the sum, and the work order charges exactly that sum per splice. Because an early fat splice keeps getting re-spliced later, joining the two shortest runs at every step keeps total spend minimal. Compute the cheapest possible bill.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array arr of rope lengths.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum total cost to join all ropes into one.

testCases.explanation: Splice 2+3=5, then 4+5=9, then 6+9=15; the bill totals 29.
Splices are 1+2=3, 3+3=6, 4+5=9 and 6+9=15 — bills of 3, 6, 9, 15 totalling 33.

starterCode.python:
import heapq

def connect_ropes(arr):
    heap = list(arr)
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    cost = 0
    while len(heap) > 1:
        a = heapq.heappop(heap)
        b = heapq.heappop(heap)
        cost += a + b
        heapq.heappush(heap, a + b)
    return cost

hintLevels: Level 1: Every rope's length is charged once per splice it survives — late splices are cheap for big ropes.
Level 2: Always fuse the two shortest current runs; a min-heap serves them instantly.
Level 3: The recurrence mirrors Huffman coding — the greedy choice is provably optimal.
